findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any database where no category matches the embed_category site setting (fresh installs and any site that never set embed_category). The INNER JOIN on site_settings.value = categories.name returns zero rows for a fresh install (embed_category default is ''), so execute(...)[0] is nil and ['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate for every new install of this version.

[BUG] The INSERT builds SQL by string interpolation of the migrated host value, so any host containing a single quote breaks the migration with a Postgres syntax error and enables SQL injection into the migration. An admin whose existing embeddable_hosts setting contained a value with an apostrophe (or any injection payload, since values came from free-text site settings) gets a failed/hijacked db:migrate during deploy.

[BUG] update calls save_host on a record looked up by params[:id] with no nil check, so a stale or invalid id raises NoMethodError on nil. PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with an id that no longer exists (e.g. the row was deleted in another admin tab) returns a 500 instead of a 404/422 the REST flow expects.

[BUG] The before_validation block calls sub! on self.host without a nil guard, so a record created without a host crashes before validation can report the error. Posting an embeddable_host payload with a missing/null host key (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil) raises NoMethodError on nilClass, returning a 500 instead of the 422 render_json_error path the controller promises.

[ADVISORY] The update action is a no-op that re-renders the unchanged @embedding, while the client's saveChanges action PUTs to it expecting persistence. Any future admin who wires settings fields into embedding.hbs and hits Save gets a silent no-op with a success response; today the client's saveChanges button (if surfaced) already does nothing server-side.

[ADVISORY] Data migration and destructive DELETE of site_settings rows are packed inside a reversible change block, so rollback drops the table without restoring the deleted embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings. An operator who runs db:rollback loses the legacy settings irrecoverably while believing the migration is reversible.

[ADVISORY] The fallback reads uncategorized_category_id from site_settings via raw SQL, but that setting's stored value is a string and the query assumes the row exists with a parsable value. On a database where the uncategorized_category_id row is absent or blank (fresh seed ordering), the [0]['value'] lookup raises the same nil-row NoMethodError as the primary path, compounding the fresh-install crash.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError for nil on any database where the 'embed_category' site_settings row is absent or no category name matches its value. On a fresh install (or any site that never set embed_category, the default ''), the INNER JOIN returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is nil, and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration for every such environment — the feature cannot be deployed. The same pattern applies to the follow-up 'uncategorized_category_id' query if that setting row was never persisted.

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddingController#update performs no update — it re-serializes @embedding without applying any params, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a silent no-op. The frontend saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}) and admins see a 'successful' save that persists nothing; any embedding-level settings edits are silently dropped with no error shown.

[BUG] update crashes with NoMethodError when params[:id] does not match a row: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil and save_host calls nil.host=. A stale host row (deleted in another tab) edited and saved by an admin yields an unhandled 500 instead of a 404/422; the destroy action at lines 18-21 has the identical nil.destroy crash on a double-delete.

[ADVISORY] The migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value directly into an INSERT statement ("... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"), so any quote in the migrated setting breaks or injects into the SQL. A site whose embeddable_hosts setting contained a single-quote or semicolon-bearing entry gets a failed migration or unintended SQL executed at deploy time by whoever authored the setting value.

[ADVISORY] The new controller specs contain no behavioral coverage — both spec files only assert the class is a subclass of AdminAdminController, while the diff adds create/update/destroy with validation, blank-category defaulting, and error rendering that nothing tests. The nil-id 500s above, the blank-category→uncategorized fallback, and render_json_error paths are all untested; the first regression in host CRUD ships silently to admins. The new embedding_serializer/admin JS client likewise have zero tests (no admin embedding JS test, no serializer spec) despite new store plural-hydration logic that only fruit fixtures exercise.

[ADVISORY] The save action silently drops the category assignment when category_id is null: it sends props.category_id = null but only after save does it set host.category via Discourse.Category.findById(null), which returns undefined and leaves the row rendering with a blank badge. An admin who clears the category chooser and saves gets no client feedback that the category was unset (the server actually coerces blank to uncategorized_category_id, so the row's displayed category is wrong until reload — it shows blank while the server stored Uncategorized).

[ADVISORY] The plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded unconditionally sets obj[pluralized] even when _lookupSubType returns null for every id, replacing the raw id array with an array of nulls and deleting the original *_ids key, so unresolvable ids are silently destroyed instead of preserved. Any payload whose side-loaded records are missing (e.g. a serializer that sends embeddable_host_ids without the side-loaded embeddable_hosts records) hydrates to [null, null] and the embedding admin page renders a blank hosts table with no error, losing the data the API did send.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the 'embed_category' site setting row does not exist. execute(...)[0]['id'] is called on an empty result set for fresh installs or sites that never set embed_category; the migration aborts and blocks every subsequent deploy, since the code does not check that a row was returned before dereferencing [0]['id'].

[BUG] destroy and update raise NoMethodError when params[:id] does not match an existing EmbeddableHost. host is nil for an unknown/deleted id, so host.destroy (destroy) and host.host = ... (update) raise NoMethodError, returning a 500 to the admin UI instead of a 404/4xx; a stale row in the browser after concurrent deletion by another admin triggers this on a routine edit.

[BUG] expandable_first_post? drops the 'embeddable hosts configured' invariant, so embedded topics now expand/truncate even when the site has zero allowed hosts. Previously a topic with a topic_embed on a site that had cleared all embeddable hosts would not be marked expandable; after this diff, expandable_first_post? is true for any topic_embed whenever embed_truncate is on, and the corresponding spec assertion was rewritten to only assert the blank-host case via a Fabricate'd host existing — the 'no hosts at all' behavior is now untested and changed, a semantic removal not traceable to the 'edit category/host relationships' intent.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that ignores its payload, while the frontend admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action PUTs to it expecting settings to persist. An admin clicking any future 'save settings' affordance on the embedding screen gets a success response while nothing is saved — a ships-inert endpoint with no requirement backing it; either implement persistence or delete the route, the PUT route in config/routes.rb, and the saveChanges action, which is dead code today.

[ADVISORY] The _hydrateEmbedded plural-suffix change is a global change to the shared store hydration pipeline, scoped into an embedding-UI feature PR with only the fruit test fixture as coverage. Every model payload containing any *_ids key now gets a pluralized hydrated array injected, changing behavior for unrelated consumers of find/findAll; a regression here breaks far more than embedding, yet no spec exercises a real (non-fixture) consumer of the plural path, making the blast radius of this feature's private infrastructure change unaudited.

[ADVISORY] basePath now string-mangles every model type (type.replace('_', '-')) to serve the single embeddable-host model, mutating shared adapter routing for all types. Any future or existing model whose underscored type name collides after dash-replacement with an ADMIN_MODELS entry is silently routed to /admin/; this global transform exists only to support one new model and belongs in the embedding-specific adapter rather than the shared rest adapter — the next change to admin model routing gets riskier because of it.

[ADVISORY] The only specs for the new admin controllers assert subclass lineage, leaving the create/update/destroy CRUD behaviors — the core of the stated feature — completely untested. A regression in save_host (e.g. the nil-host 500, or the category fallback) ships undetected; the feature 'edit category/host relationships' has zero coverage of its actual editing logic, only its class hierarchy.

[BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the site has never set embed_category, aborting the migration entirely. On any site where the 'embed_category' site setting has no row, the SELECT returns an empty result set, `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError on nil, and the whole migration (and deploy) fails; every site without embed_category configured is blocked from upgrading.

[BUG] The backfill inserts raw site-setting values verbatim via SQL, bypassing the model's scheme/path-stripping normalization, so stored hosts keep 'http://' prefixes and paths. A site with embeddable_hosts='http://discourse.org\nhttps://example.com/1234' (exactly the format the old spec used) gets rows 'http://discourse.org' and 'https://example.com/1234'; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then does lower(host) = 'discourse.org' and finds no match, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? returns false and embeds that worked before the upgrade start failing with 'invalid referer host' — a format-drift break between the write path (model before_validation) and the backfill write path (raw SQL).

[BUG] update calls save_host on a record found by id with no nil check, so a missing/already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil. PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (e.g. two admins, one deleted the row) crashes with NoMethodError in nil.host= and returns a 500 instead of a 404 error response.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record with no existence check. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id for an already-destroyed row raises NoMethodError and returns 500 rather than success/404; the client's destroyRecord promise rejects and popupAjaxError shows a server error to the admin.

[ADVISORY] The advertised PUT /admin/customize/embedding update action re-serializes @embedding without applying any params, so the controller's saveChanges is a silent no-op. The admin UI's top-level 'save changes' button (admin-embedding.js saveChanges -> embedding.update({})) fires a PUT that changes nothing while appearing to succeed; any admin relying on it loses their intent silently.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no UNIQUE index on host (and no index on category_id), so duplicate host rows are representable and every referer check scans them. Nothing prevents two admins adding 'example.com' twice; record_for_host then matches arbitrarily between the duplicates (different categories), so embedded topics land in a nondeterministic category; a unique lower(host) index would enforce the real invariant 'one record per host'.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host queries where("lower(host) = ?", host) with no index on lower(host), a non-sargable predicate run on every embed comment request. Every /embed/comments request does a full table scan with lower() on the host column; fine at 5 hosts, degrades linearly with host count on a hot unauthenticated path; an index on lower(host) (or storing downcased hosts) is required.

[ADVISORY] The new plural-id hydration maps every id through _lookupSubType with no filtering, so an id with no matching side-loaded record yields undefined entries in the hydrated array, and the `|| []` fallback can never trigger. When the serializer emits embeddable_host_ids containing an id whose record isn't side-loaded (e.g. a host deleted between fetch and hydrate, or serializer drift), the consumer gets an array containing undefined instead of a shorter list, and template code iterating the array (category-badge host.category style access) throws on undefined members.

[ADVISORY] The backfill interpolates raw setting values directly into INSERT SQL strings with no quoting or sanitization. A site_settings value containing a single quote (possible in the old free-text embeddable_hosts textarea) breaks the INSERT with a SQL syntax error mid-migration, leaving the migration half-applied; the values should go through quote/parameterized inserts.

[ADVISORY] fetch_embedding builds embeddable_hosts via EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host) with embed: :ids in the serializer, but the delete/create round-trip relies on the client mutating the in-memory list, so the embedding root is a fake singleton ('default' OpenStruct) with no persistence. The embedding 'model' can never be saved server-side (update is a no-op), making it a stand-in aggregate over EmbeddableHost rows; any future embedding-level setting added to this screen silently has nowhere to be stored, and the next developer will likely wire it to a controller that discards it.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the embed_category site setting was never saved, because site_settings rows only exist for non-default values and the code indexes into a possibly-empty result set. On a fresh install (or any site that never touched embed_category), execute(...)[0] is nil and [0]['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire migration and the deploy; the embed_category fallback branch on line 15 is never reached.

[ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings rows inside `change` with no corresponding reversible down, so a rollback permanently destroys the operator's host list and category choice. An operator who rolls back this migration to recover from a bad deploy loses their embeddable hosts configuration entirely; the data migration is not reversible even though `create_table ... force: true` is.

[ADVISORY] Host values are interpolated unescaped into raw INSERT SQL, so any legacy embeddable_hosts value containing a single quote (the old setting was free-form text) breaks the migration. A site whose legacy embeddable_hosts text contains a quote character hits a SQL syntax error mid-migration, leaving embeddable_hosts rows half-inserted before the site_settings DELETE runs.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricators were moved into a file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb while category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), i.e. the two fabricator files have swapped names/contents. Every future contributor looking for the :category fabricator in category_fabricator.rb finds the embeddable host fabricator instead, and the :embeddable_host fabricator depends on a fabricator defined in a differently-named file, making the fabricator wiring needlessly fragile and confusing to modify.

[BUG] Migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into a SQL string: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)". Any host value containing a single quote or other SQL metacharacters (the old setting was free-form host_list text with no escaping on this path) breaks the migration or executes attacker-chosen SQL against the database during deploy; string-interpolated SQL on stored values is an injection pattern even when the writer was an admin.

[BUG] update and destroy call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then invoke save_host(host) / host.destroy without checking for nil. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a nonexistent or already-deleted id passes the AdminConstraint (any staff user) and raises NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of a 404 — the destroy action also crashes rather than returning success_json, leaving the admin UI's delete flow stuck on concurrent deletes.

[BUG] save_host reads params[:embeddable_host][:host] and [:category_id] with nested hash access and no require/permit strong-parameter gating or presence check on the host key. A request whose body omits the embeddable_host key raises NoMethodError (undefined method [] for nil) yielding a 500 rather than a 4xx; category_id is also accepted unvalidated, allowing any integer (including ids of categories the staff user cannot otherwise touch, e.g. read-restricted private categories) to be silently attached as the embed target category.

[ADVISORY] Host normalization in before_validation only strips a leading scheme and the first path segment (sub! replaces once), and record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? against the URI host while stored values are never downcased before save. An admin who enters "EvilTrout.com" is stored uppercase and matched only because the query lowercases the column while the input is never lowercased on the Ruby side — the two sides of the comparison are normalized differently, so any future caller passing mixed-case input, or a stored value with a trailing slash-fragment the single sub! missed (e.g. "a.com/x/y" stores "a.com/x"), silently fails the host check and breaks embedding; the normalization-mismatch is one refactor away from an allowlist bypass or denial.

[BUG] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts the class's superclass and never invokes create, update, or destroy, so the controller's save_host parameter handling, blank category_id fallback, and render_json_error path are completely unexercised. A regression in save_host — e.g. params[:embeddable_host] being nil and raising NoMethodError, or the uncategorized fallback breaking — passes CI green while admins get 500s from the embedding admin UI; the spec passes regardless of whether any controller behavior is correct.

[BUG] The only spec for Admin::EmbeddingController asserts the class hierarchy and never tests show or update, so the fact that update (lines 13-16 of the controller) renders the serializer without persisting any changed settings is invisible to the suite. The update action silently no-ops (it never writes anything from params), yet this spec and the whole diff ship it green; an admin who edits embedding settings and saves gets stale data back with no error and no test ever fires the action to notice.

[BUG] The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer creates the condition its name describes — the embeddable_hosts site setting was deleted, and the assertion passes only because SiteSetting.embed_truncate defaults to false, making the test name a lie that verifies the wrong branch. A developer reading the suite believes a blank-host condition is covered for expandable_first_post?; in fact that condition no longer exists in the code, and the test instead redundantly re-covers the embed_truncate=false branch already tested at line 1411, giving false confidence about topic-level embedding behavior.

[ADVISORY] The 'works as expected' host_allowed? specs never test the case where the stored host was saved with a path or protocol, so the interaction between the before_validation trimming and the lower(host) lookup is only covered on one side — the old SiteSetting specs that tested 'http://' and 'https://' prefixed stored hosts were deleted rather than ported. The deleted site_setting_spec.rb cases ('works with a http host', 'works with a https host') verified that protocol-prefixed allowlist entries still match; the new model spec only creates hosts via the fabricator, so a regression in before_validation trimming (e.g. the sub! on a frozen string raising, or the path-trim regex) that would break admins who paste 'https://example.com' into the new UI goes undetected.

[BUG] The cmd_tuples > 0 guard on a SELECT is always 0 in PostgreSQL, so the guarded INSERT loop never runs while the unconditional DELETE at the end still executes. On any production PostgreSQL instance the migration deletes the site_settings rows for 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' without migrating any host rows into the new embeddable_hosts table — every site's embed allowlist and category mapping is silently destroyed with no replacement and no backup, breaking embeds site-wide.

[BUG] The embed_category lookup calls [0]['id'].to_i on a result set that is empty when no 'embed_category' row exists in site_settings (the default is '' so most sites have no stored row), raising NoMethodError on nil. The migration crashes on upgrade for every site that never set embed_category, leaving the schema half-applied and blocking the deploy; on MySQL the equivalent [0] nil access also aborts.

[BUG] The uncategorized_category_id fallback runs execute(...)[0]['value'].to_i on a possibly-empty result set (site_settings only stores non-default values), raising NoMethodError on nil. Sites with no explicit uncategorized_category_id row crash the migration mid-apply, and where the lookup yields 0 the inserted embeddable_hosts rows carry category_id = 0, an orphaned reference to a nonexistent category that breaks the new belongs_to :category and the admin UI rendering.

[BUG] Host values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT statement with no parameterization, and the new EmbeddableHost model's host trimming/normalization (stripping scheme and path) is bypassed entirely. A stored host value containing a single quote (or any value that breaks the raw SQL) aborts the migration mid-run, and even on success the migrated rows keep 'https://example.com/1234' style raw values that the model's record_for_host lower(host)= comparison will never match, so previously-working embed hosts stop being recognized after cutover.

[ADVISORY] The migration is defined with def change but performs destructive data migration (DELETE FROM site_settings) with no down path, making it irreversible. Running rake db:rollback drops the embeddable_hosts table without restoring the deleted 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' site settings rows, so operators who roll back the deploy lose the allowlist data permanently with no export or backup step anywhere in the diff.

[BUG] The INSERT omits the model's before_validation normalization and validates_format_of, so backfilled rows are not subject to the same integrity constraints the application enforces. Junk/whitespace/URL-prefixed rows land in embeddable_hosts with no validation, and record_for_host's exact lower(host)= match then fails against them, silently breaking embeds for hosts that worked under the old substring/URI-host-matching logic in SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?.

[ADVISORY] create_table uses force: true for the embeddable_hosts table. If this table name ever collides (e.g. re-running or a plugin created a table of the same name), the migration silently drops the pre-existing table and its data before recreating it empty.

[BUG] update calls save_host on a nil host when params[:id] does not match a record. EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil for a stale/unknown id (e.g. the row was deleted in another tab or an admin edits a deleted host), save_host then executes nil.host = ... and raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 where the API contract for a missing admin resource expects 404/4xx; the same crash hits destroy at line 17 via nil.destroy.

[ADVISORY] destroyRecord().then(...) has no .catch rejection handler, unlike the save() action which uses popupAjaxError. When the DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id request fails (network error, 500, session expiry), the promise rejection is silently swallowed: the admin sees the confirm dialog close and the host stays in the list with no error message, and cannot distinguish 'delete failed' from a UI bug; retrying gives no feedback either.

[ADVISORY] The update action (PUT /customize/embedding) performs no save of anything — it only re-fetches via fetch_embedding and re-serializes — yet returns a success response. Any client that PUTs to /customize/embedding gets HTTP success with a serialized payload while zero work is done; combined with the controller's saveChanges() action calling embedding.update({}) (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 5) this is a silent no-op success path, and the only reason it is unexploited is that embedding.hbs never renders a save button — dead API surface that will mislead the first future caller into thinking it persisted.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) returns nil when the embedded URL's host is not in the table (or the URL is malformed), and category: eh.try(:category_id) then silently passes nil to PostCreator with no log. Topics imported from feeds whose URL does not match any EmbeddableHost are silently created with no category (falling back to whatever PostCreator's nil-category default is) instead of the previously configured embed_category — a silent behavior change in which category embedded content lands in, invisible to the operator until they notice misplaced topics.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

When the serializer emits embeddable_host_ids containing an id whose record isn't side-loaded (e.g. a host deleted between fetch and hydrate, or serializer drift), the consumer gets an array containing undefined instead of a shorter list, and template code iterating the array (category-badge host.category style access) throws on undefined members.

Because `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy), the `|| []` fallback can never run, and any missing side-loaded record will result in `undefined` entries in the hydrated array. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Migration interpolates the raw embeddable_hosts setting value into a SQL string: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly indexes `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (no `require`/presence guard). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host normalization in before_validation only strips a leading scheme and the first path segment (sub! replaces once), and record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? against the URI host while stored values are never downcased before save. An admin who enters "EvilTrout.com" is stored uppercase and matched only because the query lowercases the column while the input is never lowercased on the Ruby side — the two sides of the comparison are normalized differently, so any future caller passing mixed-case input, or a stored value with a trailing slash-fragment the single sub! missed (e.g. "a.com/x/y" stores "a.com/x"), silently fails the host check and breaks embedding; the normalization-mismatch is one refactor away from an allowlist bypass or denial.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: `record_for_host` lowercases the DB column (`lower(host)`) but does not consistently normalize/lowercase the input host parameter, so mixed-case hosts can fail to match despite intending case-insensitive comparison. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cmd_tuples > 0 guard on a SELECT is always 0 in PostgreSQL, so the guarded INSERT loop never runs while the unconditional DELETE at the end still executes. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The INSERT omits the model's before_validation normalization and validates_format_of, so backfilled rows are not subject to the same integrity constraints the application enforces. Junk/whitespace/URL-prefixed rows land in embeddable_hosts with no validation, and record_for_host's exact lower(host)= match then fails against them, silently breaking embeds for hosts that worked under the old substring/URI-host-matching logic in SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?.

VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` for each line from the old `site_settings` value (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb).
